title: Double a Number Represented as a Linked List
summary: Given a non-empty linked list representing a non-negative integer without leading zeroes, return the head of the linked list after doubling the integer.
statement: Given a non-empty linked list representing a non-negative integer without leading zeroes, return the head of the linked list after doubling the integer.
constraints: Digits appear most-significant first with no leading zero.
Return the decimal linked list representing exactly twice the input number.
hints: Carry flows from the least-significant tail toward the head.
Use postorder recursion to process next nodes before the current digit.
Return carry from each recursive call; prepend a node if the head produces carry.
Each node receives exactly its doubled digit plus the carry from all less-significant digits.
editorial: Each node receives exactly its doubled digit plus the carry from all less-significant digits.

tests.explanation: Twice 189 is 378, so the returned digits are 3,7,8.
Twice 999 is 1998 and needs a new leading node.
